Subject: I ran my first marathon!

Hey [Name],  

I wanted to tell you I ran my first marathon last Sunday. It was crazy hard, but I did it. I didn’t run the whole time — I walked a lot — but I kept going. I thought about you a bunch, actually. You always said running was about showing up, not about being fast. So I showed up.  

I’m not sure if I’ll ever run another one, but I’m glad I did. It made me feel like I could do more than I thought. Thanks for saying that.  

Let me know if you want to run one. Maybe we can do it together.  

Take care,  
[Your Name]

Running your first marathon is a big deal. It’s not just about running 26 miles — it’s about training for it, getting ready for it, and then doing it. You have to build up your legs, your lungs, your heart. You have to run every day, even when you don’t feel like it. You have to eat right, sleep enough, and not get sick. You have to plan the race, too — what you’ll wear, what you’ll eat when you’re halfway, what you’ll do when you feel like giving up.

You’ll feel like you can’t do it. You’ll think you’re going to fall down. You’ll think you’re going to cry. But you don’t. You keep going. You keep putting one foot in front of the other. You don’t know how you do it, but you do. You finish. And when you finish, you feel like you’ve done something. You’ve done something hard, and you did it.

You’ll remember the people who helped you. The people who ran with you, or who sent you messages. You’ll remember the people who told you you could do it. You’ll remember the miles you ran, and the days you didn’t feel like running. You’ll remember the time you almost gave up, but you didn’t. You’ll remember the way your legs felt, and how your lungs burned, and how your heart was going to pop. But you didn’t stop. You kept going.

You’ll feel proud. You’ll feel like you’ve got something. You’ll feel like you can do more. You’ll want to run again. You’ll want to run more. You’ll want to run farther. You’ll want to run faster. You’ll want to run better.

You’ll think about the next time. You’ll think about the next race. You’ll think about the next thing you can do. You’ll think about the next thing you can try. You’ll think about the next thing you can do. You’ll think about the next thing you can do.

You’ll feel like you can do it. You’ll feel like you can do it. You’ll feel like you can do it.

I just ran my first marathon. It wasn’t perfect. I walked a lot. I cried a lot. But I finished. And that’s what matters.  

I trained for 12 weeks. Some days I felt like I could run forever. Other days I wanted to quit. I had to keep showing up. Even when my legs hurt. Even when my head hurt.  

I thought about all the people who helped me. My friends who kept me going when I didn’t want to. My family who didn’t get why I was doing it. My coach who told me to keep running.  

The last mile was the hardest. I thought I was going to fall. But I kept going.  

When I crossed the line, I didn’t feel like I won. I felt like I did it.  

It’s not about the time. It’s about the miles. It’s about the days you don’t want to run. It’s about the people who help you.  

I’m proud of myself. I’m not done. I’ll keep running.

Keeping a monthly budget is one of the simplest things you can do to feel in control of your money. It doesn’t have to be complicated. You just need to track your income and your expenses, and make sure you’re not spending more than you have.

Start by writing down how much money you get each month. That’s your income. Then write down everything you spend. Rent, groceries, bills, gas, food out, clothes, maybe a movie or a concert. Add it all up. If the total is more than your income, you’re in trouble. If it’s less, you have money left over. That’s good.

You can use a spreadsheet or a notebook. Some people use apps. It doesn’t matter. What matters is that you do it every day. You look at your money and you decide where it goes.

You can make a list of what you need and what you want. The needs are the basics. The wants are the things you can live without. You put the needs first. Then you see if you have money left for the wants. If not, you cut the wants.

You can also make a list of things you don’t need. Maybe you can stop buying coffee every day. Maybe you can wait a week before buying something. You can save money by not buying things you don’t need.

When you do this every month, you start to see where your money goes. You start to know what you can change. You start to feel like you’re in charge.

It’s not about being perfect. It’s about trying. It’s about making sure you don’t spend more than you have. That’s how you get money for the things you need. That’s how you save some for the things you want. That’s how you feel like you’re not running out of money every day.

You can do this. You just have to start. You just have to write down the numbers. Then you see what you can change. Then you make a plan. Then you stick with it. Then you feel like you’re in control.

Keeping a monthly budget is like having a plan for your money so you don’t run out before the month is over. It helps you know where your money goes and if you’re spending too much on things that don’t matter. You start by adding up all the money you get each month, like your paycheck or money from other jobs. Then you list all the things you have to pay for, like rent, food, bills, and maybe a phone plan. That’s your fixed costs. Then you list the things you might spend money on, like going out to eat or buying something you don’t really need. That’s your variable costs.

You write down all the money you have and all the money you spend. If you have more money than you spend, you can save some. If you spend more, you have to make sure you don’t go into debt. You can use a notebook or a phone app to keep track. Some people like to write down all the money they get and all the money they spend, and then see if they have extra. If they do, they put it in a savings jar. If they don’t, they have to cut back on some things.

It’s not always easy. You might have to say no to something you want. But if you do it every month, you get used to it. You start to know what’s important and what’s not. You can use the money you save to buy something bigger later, like a new phone or a trip. You don’t have to wait for a long time. You just keep doing it every month.

A budget helps you not get surprised when the money runs out. It helps you not get into trouble with the bank. It helps you feel like you’re in control. You can still have fun, but you know you’ll have money for it. You can go out to eat once in a while, but you don’t spend all the money. You can buy a new shirt, but you don’t buy two. You just do it every month. It’s like a plan for your money. You don’t have to be perfect. You just have to do it every month. That’s how you save money. That’s how you don’t run out.

Keeping a monthly budget doesn’t have to be boring. It’s just a way to make sure your money goes where it needs to. You can start by listing all your bills—rent, utilities, food, gas. Then you list all your money coming in—paycheck, side gigs, maybe some cash from selling stuff. Then you see where you can cut back. Maybe you eat out less. Maybe you buy cheaper clothes. You can save a little every month. It’s not about being perfect. It’s about being in control. And when you’re in control, you can do things you want. Like go on vacation. Or buy a new phone. Or just feel safe. A budget helps you know what’s coming. It helps you plan. It helps you not worry about money. It’s not magic. It’s just math. But it works. And when you do it, you feel better. Like you’re not just surviving. You’re living. And that’s the point. You want to live. So you make sure your money does too.

Keeping a monthly budget is like having a map in a storm. It doesn’t stop the rain, but it helps you know where you’re going. I think people say they don’t like budgets because they feel like they’re giving up something. But a budget isn’t about giving up. It’s about knowing what you’re doing with your money. You don’t have to be perfect. You just have to be honest. You have to say, “This is what I have. This is what I need. This is what I want.” And then you decide which is more important.

I think people think budgets are for people who don’t have money. But I think they’re for people who have money and want to make sure they don’t spend it all. You don’t have to be rich to need a budget. You just have to be careful. You have to be careful about the things that cost nothing but take a lot of time. Like watching TV. Or scrolling on your phone. You have to make sure you’re not doing that all the time. You have to make sure you’re not spending money on things that don’t matter. You have to make sure you’re saving some for the future. Even if it’s just a little.

I think people think budgets are a way to control them. But they’re not. They’re a way to stop them from being surprised. Like when you get a bill and you didn’t have money for it. You didn’t have a budget. You didn’t know where the money went. You didn’t know what you were doing. You just had to pay it. And then you had to think about it. But if you had a budget, you’d know. You’d know where the money was. You’d know where it went. You’d know you had to save some. You’d know you had to buy something else. You’d know you had to do something. You’d know you had to be careful.

A budget is like a plan. It’s not a plan to make you happy. It’s a plan to make you not worry. It’s a plan to make you not feel like you’re losing everything. It’s a plan to make you feel like you’re in control. And that’s the best part. You don’t have to be rich. You just have to be careful. You just have to be honest. You just have to be sure. You just have to know where the money is.

Board games are a kind of game you play with a group of people, usually on a table. You move pieces around, or roll dice, or pick cards. You try to win by getting points or making the other people lose. Some games are about luck, like rolling dice and hoping for a good number. Some are about thinking, like trying to plan ahead so you can get what you want. Some are about talking, like trying to get people to agree with you. Some are about making things happen, like moving your piece around the board and trying to get to the end first.
